      longer available" words) and never an image-generation reference
      (`media-reference-images.ts`, `selectBlockedImageUrls` on the lookup's
      connection). `publish_blog` refuses a draft whose title or address is a
      told-blocked post's (`mink_blog_blocked`). The redesign snapshot and the
      personalisation context leave every blocked product, collection and page
      out, told or not (a blocked page stays as `skipped: "policy"`, so it is
      never recreated), and a coupon campaign's brand snapshot carries a null
      logo when the logo is blocked. Not marked, on purpose:
      `list_current_offers` and the drafting checkpoint reads. ⚠ A redesign may
      still create an item named like a blocked one, and under an untold block
      Mink cannot refuse without revealing it (owner question).
    - **★ WHO CAN DO WHAT** (design 3.10): every operator sees everything but
      archived contents, logs and handles complaints, blocks items (a store's
      own request included), replies, retries, marks a theme file removed;
      only a superadmin keeps a block from the store or tells it later,
      suspends a whole store, lifts any block (D19, D22), opens or keeps an
      archived copy, and holds a store. Every action re-checks
      (`getPlatformViewer`); a non-operator gets "Only a StoreMink operator can
      block content." for every one.
    - **Alerts** (D12, production step P4): `docs/monitoring.md` 25 to 28 on
      `moderation: complaint ` (prefix), `moderation: follow-up failed`
      (prefix: production `logError` appends the stack), the absence of
      `moderation: follow-ups ran` for 10 minutes, and the `send-emails`
      schedule's failed attempts; production step P8 makes the support mailbox
      wake someone for an emailed complaint.
    - **⚠ Not built, or left open:** the public complaint form (D11); pausing
      the other retention sweeps for a held store (D15); the policy sentences of
      design 13 (the next Terms, Privacy and Acceptable Use versions); the
      re-upload refusal for videos; production steps P1 (is Cloud CDN on), P2,
      P3 (bucket lifecycle and versioning), P4 to P8. Owner questions: the
      merchant's DASHBOARD invoice still prints a blocked logo
      (`loadInvoiceByStore`); suspended owners still receive notices
      (`storeOwnerEmails`); a blocked Refine publish says the photo "will
      appear in a few minutes"; a store over 256 MiB cannot be suspended from
      the console; Mink AI's WhatsApp drafts written before a block may still
      name the product (the merchant reviews every draft, R6).
    - **Tests.** Pure: `kinds`, `deadlines`, `media-key`, `media-refs`, `copy`
      (every sentence, with no long dash, square bracket, credit figure or
      word for the POS other than "POS"), `archive-paths`. Server: `record`, `blocked-objects`, `mask`,
      `upload-guard`, `placeholder`, `storage`, `complaints`, `holds`,
      `author-blocks`, `notify`, `snapshot`, `store-content`, `block`,
      `archive`, `console-read`, `follow-ups`, `retention`, `merchant`,
      `migration` (the 0269 shape), `mask-coverage`, and beside them
      `lib/storage/store-objects.test.ts`,
      `lib/storage/upload-guard-coverage.test.ts`,
      `lib/checkout/product-reads.test.ts`, `lib/offers/resolve.test.ts` and
      `lib/offers/cart.test.ts` (which prices through the real
      `loadLiveOffers`, the POS case included), `lib/shipping/product-delivery.test.ts`,
      `lib/legal/store-consent.test.ts`, `lib/email/takedown-emails.test.ts`,
      `app/actions/takedown-actions.test.ts`, the two archive route tests, the
      console page tests, `platform.test.ts`, the notice page tests,
      `store-notice-actions.test.ts`, `app/dashboard/takedown-badge-css.test.ts`,
      `proxy.test.ts`, the og-image route test and `app/sitemap.test.ts`.
      Opt-in local suites (`MODERATION_LOCAL_TEST=1`, `storemink_local` on
      5544, one rolled-back transaction each, a savepoint per case, the code as
      `app_service`, `fetch` and every storage client throwing):
      `lib/moderation/schema.local.test.ts` (design 4.4's probes P1 to P18, V1,
      V2, plan A10 and A11; it takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks in savepoints, so
      run it alone), `shopper-reads`, `complaints`, `block`, `archive`
      (`DB_NAME` stubbed to `storemink_local`), `follow-ups` (block erasure,
      the claims against the real schema) and
      `lib/storefront/queries.local.test.ts`.

46. **Placeholders and descriptions are short and general (owner's rule,
    31 Oct 2026).** The owner found example data from a real store in
    placeholders everywhere ("Cold-pressed mustard and groundnut oils for
    families who cook at home", "Pressed in our own mill in Faridkot since
    1998") and paragraph descriptions on every card, dialog and field.
    - **A placeholder is kept only when it is short, general and useful:** a
      search or filter box ("Search products"), a message composer ("Message
      Mink AI"), or a pure format cue that cannot be mistaken for real data
      ("https://", "0.00"). Never an example drawn from a store, product,
      person, place, number or date, never the label repeated, never an
      instruction. A control whose placeholder was its only name gets a label
      or an `aria-label`.
    - **A description is one sentence, two at most, never more than two
      rendered lines**, and none at all when the heading already says it:
      page subtitles, card and dialog descriptions, settings toggles, empty
      states. A field hint stays only when it must be read before typing and
      fits one line. Footnote paragraphs are deleted. Warnings about money or
      irreversible actions stay, cut to the essential sentence.
    - **Guidance a merchant needs now and then goes behind the "i" button**
      (`components/ui/info-tip.tsx`, placed BESIDE the label, never inside it,
      so the field's accessible name is unchanged), in one or two short
      sentences. The Storefront page's Customise storefront dialog is the
      reference.
    - **Dialogs share one look** (`components/ui/dialog.tsx`): actions in
      `DialogFooter`, no per-dialog title or description typography, and a
      different padding only through `[--dialog-pad:…]`.
    - Out of scope, deliberately: marketing page copy, Help Centre articles,
      emails, legal and consent text, `lib/billing/tax-copy.ts` and
      `lib/moderation/copy.ts` (pinned wording), theme definitions and Mink
      AI prompts. No merchant step changes, so no Help Centre update; button
      labels, headings and field labels were kept, because Mink AI's spotlight
      (`lib/mink/guide-targets.ts`), tests and Help guides name them.

## 6. Commands

> **Dev feels slow?** See `docs/local-dev-performance.md`. September's saved
> trace contains 60 s login compilation and 43 s builder compilation: August's
> fast timings must not be treated as a permanent diagnosis. The 8 GB Mac also
> showed 6.4 GB swap used and 3.3 GB compressed RAM. Check current memory pressure
> and separate compile time from render/database time. The runner limits V8's
> old space, not total process memory. Warm caches are preserved by default;
> `DEV_CACHE_MAX_MB` opts into size-based dev-cache rotation, and `dev:reset` is
> for cache recovery, not routine speed tuning. `dev:all:webpack` provides an
> explicit Webpack command with the same proxy and V8 heap policy. On ≤12 GB
> RAM the runner now selects Webpack automatically; `dev:all:turbo` opts back in
> to Turbopack. Development-only Webpack configuration limits parallel module
> processing to 8 per compiler on ≤12 GB RAM (32 above; override through
> `DEV_WEBPACK_PARALLELISM`) and disables output path comments. On ≤12 GB,
> on-demand entries use Next's 60 s/five-page defaults to reduce eviction and
> repeat compilation during dashboard navigation. Mink history and the bell
> use separate modules so small reads do not compile unrelated write tooling.
> The dashboard and operator chrome request JetBrains Mono as one variable
> face, avoiding the fixed 400/500 font query failure in Next 16.3.8 Turbopack.
> The font family and CSS variables are preserved. Next's source maps, loaders,
> chunking and caches are preserved. Production
> config has no custom Webpack callback. See the performance doc for sources
> and measured results; this is a memory/throughput tradeoff, not a RAM ceiling.
> This is internal development tooling; customer flows and Help Centre content
> are unchanged.
> ★ 2026-10-08: measured again on the 8 GB M2 Air — swap 15.2 GB of 16 GB used
> before the dev server started, Chrome 83 renderers, the editor's plugin host
> 1 GB, `next-server` 2.2 GB almost entirely paged out. The hangs are swap
> thrashing and the "Rendering" badge is the dashboard's own 20-second list
> polling. Dev now sets `webpackMemoryOptimizations` on ≤12 GB machines, polls
> three times slower, and the runner's swap warning names the memory holders.
> Full table: `docs/local-dev-performance.md` § October 8.
> ★ When Turbopack IS the bundler on a small machine, its dev filesystem cache
> (a default since Next 16.1) is switched off: its periodic write and compaction
> of a multi-GB `.next/dev/cache` competes with the swap file for one SSD, and was
> measured blocking a request for **101 seconds of framework time against 1.5 s of
> application code**. `--fs-cache` forces it back on. ★★ When a request looks slow,
> read its `next.js:` versus `application-code:` split before suspecting the
> database — that one number separates a bundler-cache stall from the ~46 ms
> Mumbai round trip.

```bash
npm run dev         # Webpack on ≤12 GB RAM, Turbopack above; 2 GB heap on ≤12 GB,
                    #   3 GB on ≤20 GB, uncapped above; test stores via {slug}.localhost:3000
npm run dev:webpack # explicit Webpack; same V8 heap policy
npm run dev:all:webpack # explicit Webpack + Cloud SQL proxy
npm run dev:turbo   # explicit Turbopack (also works on low-memory machines)
npm run dev:all:turbo # explicit Turbopack + Cloud SQL proxy
npm run dev:lean    # force the 2 GB heap regardless of detected machine memory
npm run dev:full    # explicitly disable the heap cap (for high-memory machines/debugging)
npm run dev:reset   # delete generated .next/dev only; next launch recompiles cold once
npm run dev -- --fs-cache     # force Turbopack's dev filesystem cache ON  (DEV_FS_CACHE=1)
npm run dev -- --no-fs-cache  # force it OFF (DEV_FS_CACHE=0); default is OFF on ≤12 GB RAM
npm run dev:all     # ↑ dev + the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy together (concurrently) — one command
npm run dev:all:lean # ↑ force the 2 GB heap + proxy (normally identical on this 8 GB Mac)
npm run dev:all:full # ↑ uncapped dev + proxy
npm run db:local:start  # ★ start the LOCAL dev Postgres (Homebrew @17, port 5544)
npm run db:local:status # cluster state + storemink_local table count
npm run db:local:sync   # rebuild storemink_local from staging (add -- --schema-only to skip data)
npm run db:local:psql   # psql into storemink_local
npm run themes:remove-samples # dry run: theme samples older installs left (§11).
                    #   Write: `-- --commit --confirm-database <DB_NAME>`;
                    #   one store: `-- --store <slug>`
npm run db:local:stop   # stop the cluster
npm run db:drift:local  # ★ has DDL reached this database without the runner?
npm run db:drift:staging #   same for staging (via the proxy; needs gcloud auth for the secret)
npm run db:drift:prod   #   and production. Exit 0 = clean, 1 = drift or stale baseline.
                    #   After a real migration: re-run with `-- --update-baseline <env>`
                    #   and COMMIT drizzle/migrations/schema-fingerprint.json in the
                    #   same change, or the detector cannot tell the next manual DDL
                    #   from the migration you just applied.
npm run db:migrate:local # ledger status/apply against --environment local (ENV_DATABASES.local
                    #   is null, so there is no database-name guard). A local database that
                    #   also carries another branch's migrations needs
                    #   `-- apply --allow-unknown local` (local only; staging/prod refuse)
                    #   ★ With .env.local present the app uses the LOCAL database and you run
                    #   `npm run dev`, NOT `dev:all` — there is no proxy to start. Warm renders
                    #   drop from ~1.2 s of application-code to ~1-3 ms per query. Rationale,
                    #   measurements and the Identity-Platform pairing warning are in
                    #   docs/local-dev-performance.md.
                    # ★★ ALL SIX db:migrate:* / db:drift:* SCRIPTS PIN DB_HOST AND DB_PORT
                    #   (staging and prod at 127.0.0.1:6543 via the proxy, local at
                    #   127.0.0.1:5544). None of them may inherit host/port from the env
                    #   files, and the two failure directions are different:
                    #   • staging/prod set DB_NAME but used to inherit host/port, so an
                    #     .env.local pointing at a local cluster redirected them. That failed
                    #     safely ONLY because no local database carried those names — and the
                    #     environment guard compares the database NAME, not the host, so a
                    #     local database called `storemink` would let `db:migrate:prod apply`
                    #     write to LOCAL while reporting success as production.
                    #   • the LOCAL scripts pinned nothing at all, and `ENV_DATABASES.local`
                    #     is null, so there is NO name guard on that side either. Delete
                    #     .env.local and `db:migrate:local apply` would have written to
                    #     storemink_staging while calling itself local — the more likely
                    #     accident, since deleting .env.local is the documented way to look
                    #     at staging. Verified after pinning by moving .env.local aside: it
                    #     still reports database=storemink_local.
npm run db:proxy    # just the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy → staging DB on localhost:6543 (needs
                    #   `gcloud auth application-default login` once for ADC). Points at the
                    #   `storemink-prod-db` INSTANCE; local dev uses its `storemink_staging`
                    #   DATABASE (set DB_NAME=storemink_staging in .env — staging & prod are
                    #   two databases in one instance, see §7). Must be running (else
                    #   lookupStoreByHost → ECONNREFUSED/ECONNRESET). Runs with
                    #   `--run-connection-test` so an expired/reauth-needed ADC token kills the
                    #   proxy at startup (dev:all then `--kill-others-on-fail`s the dev server)
                    #   instead of listening and RESETTING every query — a silent proxy makes
                    #   the dashboard render "No access to this dashboard".
npm run build       # production build
npm run lint        # eslint
npm run typecheck   # next typegen, then strict tsc --noEmit with a 4 GiB heap;
                    # tsconfig.typecheck.json validates fresh production route types
                    # without reading mutable .next/dev generated declarations.
npm run test        # vitest run --coverage
npm run test:shuffle # ★ the SAME suite in a different (fixed-seed) order — the only
                    #   thing that catches order-dependent tests. CI runs it.
npm run test:watch  # vitest watch
npm run email:gallery # render every email into .email-gallery/ (open index.html)
npm run format      # prettier --write
npm run theme-studio:model-check -- --dry-run # resolve the two task-scoped
                    #   Gemini model ids without network; without --dry-run it calls the
                    #   FREE countTokens endpoint per model (needs ADC + a project id)
npm run theme-studio:eval # Phase 0 golden set through the generation pipeline, offline
                    #   (fake provider, grades nothing). A paid live run needs
                    #   `-- --live --model=gemini-3.8-flash --max-usd=5 --yes`
npm run revamp:priority-test -- --max-usd=8 --label=capacity # Offline dry run,
                    #   default 54 calls planned, no credentials/services read.
                    #   --lanes/--ladders select work. --live --yes spends and
                    #   requires explicit approval; see docs/mink-revamp-speed.md.
```

## 7. Environments / external services

Voice transport: `MINK_SARVAM_TTS_TRANSPORT=rest` rolls Bulbul back to the
complete-clip endpoint. Unset (default) uses HTTP streaming. There is no paid
retry between transports. Live staging validation is required before rollout;
see `docs/mink-sarvam-realtime-audit-2026-10-27.md` for existing latency evidence.

- **Google Cloud is the whole backend**: Postgres on Cloud SQL (`lib/db`), auth
  on Identity Platform (`lib/auth`), media on Cloud Storage (`lib/storage`,
  GCS-only), hosting on Cloud Run, schedules in Cloud Scheduler. App-side
  password floor is 8 chars (`app/platform/signup/page.tsx`).
- **Identity Platform (Firebase Auth) — the auth provider (GCP Phase 6).** All
  auth goes through `lib/auth/*` (see §4). **ENV:**
  - **One Identity Platform project PER ENVIRONMENT, paired with that env's Cloud
    SQL DATABASE.** Staging and prod now share ONE Cloud SQL INSTANCE
    (`storemink-prod-db`) as two databases — `storemink_staging` (staging + local
    dev) and `storemink` (prod); there is no separate staging instance anymore.
    The project↔database pairing is still mandatory because `admins.id`/`users.id`
    in Cloud SQL ARE the Firebase uid — crossing them (e.g. the staging database +
    the prod project) makes `getServerUser` return uids with no matching row →
    everything reads as signed-out. So the `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*` (and server SA)
    values DIFFER per environment:
    | env | Cloud SQL database (`DB_NAME`, all in `storemink-prod-db`) | Firebase/IP project | keys |
    | ---------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ----------- |
    | local dev | `storemink_staging` | **staging** project | staging |
    | staging | `storemink_staging` | **staging** project | staging |
    | dev (deployed) | `storemink_staging` | **staging** project | staging |
    | production | `storemink` | **prod** project | prod |
    Local dev uses the STAGING project (its database holds staging-project uids).
    The web `apiKey` is NOT a secret — it's a public project id; separate projects
    are about ISOLATING test users/SMS from prod, not secrecy. The database is
    selected purely by `DB_NAME` (`lib/db/client.ts`), so a wrong `DB_NAME` on a
    shared instance is the one thing that would cross staging and prod — the
    deploy config guards this (see `docs/gcp-ci-cd.md`), and hardening to a
    restricted `app_staging` role is a documented pre-launch step.
  - **Server (Admin SDK)**: `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` + `FIREBASE_CLIENT_EMAIL` +
    `FIREBASE_PRIVATE_KEY` (service account; `\n`-escaped key), OR Application
    Default Credentials (automatic on Cloud Run; locally set
    `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` to a SA key file, or `GCP_PROJECT_ID` — either
    triggers the ADC path). `FIREBASE_API_KEY` (web API key) is ALSO read
    server-side for the change-password re-verify (the REST
    `accounts:signInWithPassword` call — the Admin SDK can't check a password).
  - **Client (Web SDK)**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `_AUTH_DOMAIN`,
    `_PROJECT_ID`, `_STORAGE_BUCKET`, `_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID`, `_APP_ID` (the public
    Firebase web config — not secret).
  - **Console setup (Identity Platform, per project — NOT in code):**
    - **Providers**: enable **Email/Password**, **Email link (passwordless)** (the
      operator login uses it), **Google**, and **Phone**. Phone requires
      **reCAPTCHA** (the app uses an invisible `RecaptchaVerifier`) — this also
      covers the anti-abuse / SMS-pumping hardening.
    - **Google**: a Google Cloud OAuth **Web** client; put its client id/secret on
      the Google provider. Sign-in uses `signInWithPopup` (no callback route), so
      no app redirect URIs go into Google — only Firebase's own auth handler does.
    - **Authorized domains** (Authentication → Settings): list every host the app
      runs on so popup + email-link work — `localhost` and `storemink.com` (+ the
      staging equivalents). For POPUPS one entry covers every subdomain (the SDK
      matches `^(.+\.<entry>|<entry>)$`), but **PHONE CODES need every EXACT
      host listed** — `CAPTCHA_CHECK_FAILED : Hostname match not found`
      otherwise — and **Firebase rejects wildcards**. The app maintains the
      exact entries itself: each store's subdomain from signup, each custom
      domain's apex + www from go-live, and an hourly repair pass (§30,
      `lib/auth/authorized-domains.ts`). Without them, phone sign-in fails on
      that store and "Continue with Google" is dead on a merchant's own
      domain while email+password still works. There is NO per-path
      redirect-URL list; popup / email-link just need the domain
      authorized. Cross-subdomain session cookies still span `.storemink.com`
      (set by `/api/auth/session`), so the signup→dashboard handoff works across
      subdomains on real domains (flaky on `localhost`, as before).
  - **User import (done once, at the move to Identity Platform)**: users were
    imported with `admin.auth().importUsers()`, preserving each **uid** and
    bcrypt hash (no password resets), so an `admins.id` / `users.id` holds
    either an imported uuid-shaped uid or a Firebase uid (both `text`); every
    FK and the `app.current_user_id` GUC work with zero remapping.
- **Cloud Run + Cloud Scheduler**: hosting on Cloud Run behind the External
  Application Load Balancer, whose certificate map serves `storemink.com`, the
  `*.storemink.com` store subdomains and verified custom domains (§3 Host
  routing); cron jobs in Cloud Scheduler (`docs/cron-jobs.md`); deploys in
  `docs/gcp-ci-cd.md`. ★ CLIENT IP: the load balancer APPENDS
  `<client-ip>,<lb-ip>` to any `X-Forwarded-For` a caller sends, so
  `lib/client-ip.ts` reads that header from the RIGHT: it finds the rightmost
  `DOMAIN_LB_IP` (the forwarding-rule address cloudbuild.yaml sets on every web
  revision; searching keeps the rule right if Google adds a hop after it) and
  takes the entry before it, the address the load balancer saw; a single entry
  (local dev, a direct `*.run.app` request) is used as it is.
  Every per-IP rate limit (`clientIp` re-exported by `lib/rate-limit.ts`), the
  POS audit trail, the consent records (`lib/legal/store.ts`,
  `lib/legal/store-consent.ts`) and the storefront visitor key use it;
  `x-real-ip` is never read. `lib/client-ip.test.ts` pins forged headers and
  that the deploy still passes `DOMAIN_LB_IP`. ⚠ `DOMAIN_LB_IP` is the
  anchor: if it is empty or wrong, or the request came through another
  frontend (an IPv6 forwarding rule), the FIRST entry is used, the rule before
  26 Oct 2026: forgeable, but every visitor keeps a key of their own (taking
  the rightmost would give everyone the frontend's address as ONE key and let
  one busy store lock every visitor out). On Cloud Run the first such request
  per instance logs `client-ip: X-Forwarded-For does not end in DOMAIN_LB_IP`
  (ERROR). So DNS stays A-record only until the code accepts an IPv6 frontend. A visitor
  behind a proxy that adds its own entry (a data-saver browser, an office
  proxy, a CDN in front of a merchant's domain) is keyed by that proxy's
  address, shared with everyone behind it.
- **Cloud Monitoring (production alerting, 2026-10-23, owner-approved)**: 15
  alert policies (plus five Theme Studio log alerts defined in the script,
  plan P6, applied after the Theme Studio release with the owner's OK, step
  A1, and two refund log alerts, "Billing: a refund to a merchant failed"
  and "Billing: refunds waiting more than a day", `docs/monitoring.md` 21
  and 22, at most one email an hour each, applied as the owner's production
  step after the refunds release, and two GST log alerts, "Billing: renewals
  cannot read the GST settings" and "Billing: a captured payment's invoice is
  still a draft", `docs/monitoring.md` 23 and 24, applied by the owner after
  the GST release, and the four takedown alerts, `docs/monitoring.md` 25 to 28,
  watching the every-minute takedown follow-ups and the `send-emails`
  schedule, applied by the owner after the takedown release: 28 policies
  defined), three uptime checks (storemink.com, a merchant store and its
  dashboard login, every 60 s from USA, Europe and Asia Pacific), the
  log-based counter `mink_chat_run_failures` (and, defined for the takedown
  release, `moderation_followups_ran`) and one email channel ("StoreMink
  owner email"; the address is never in the repo), all in storemink-prod,
  labelled `managed-by=storemink-alerts` and created by
  `scripts/prod-monitoring.py`. The app reads none of it and no environment
  variable configures it. What each alert means and what to check first:
  **`docs/monitoring.md`**. ⚠ The server, memory and log alerts watch
  `storemink-web-prod` only and the database alerts the shared
  `storemink-prod-db` instance, so the dev service is not watched; the five
  Theme Studio alerts also match the private Theme Studio workers, the
  capture job and the Theme Studio schedules' own attempt log (the Google AI
  and Cloud Run quota alerts cover the whole project); the storemink-staging
  project has no alerts.
- **Resend**: transactional email + custom-domain DNS verification. Delivery
  webhooks post to `/api/webhooks/resend` and need **`RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`**
  (Svix signing secret) plus the endpoint registered in the Resend dashboard,
  subscribed to `email.bounced` + `email.complained` — without it bounces are
  never learned and dead addresses are mailed forever (§22). It is **per
  ENDPOINT, therefore per env** (`_RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET_SECRET` in
  `cloudbuild.yaml` → `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET_{STAGING,PROD}`), unlike
  `RESEND_API_KEY`, which is one account-wide key. It went unwired on Cloud Run
  until 2026-08-01, so the whole suppression half of §24 was inert — the route
  degrades by logging and dropping the event, which is the failure you don't
  notice. Registration + secret creation runbook: `docs/gcp-ci-cd.md`.
- **Google Cloud Storage** (media, GCP migration Phase 3 — `lib/storage/gcs.ts`):
  when **`GCS_BUCKET`** is set, new image/video uploads go to that GCS bucket
  (public by link: `allUsers` holds `roles/storage.legacyObjectReader`, get
  without list, once owner step P1 has run; uniform bucket-level access) and
  public URLs are
  `https://storage.googleapis.com/<bucket>/<path>`. Uploads are **GCS-only**
  (require `GCS_BUCKET`). Auth via ADC (Cloud Run default SA, or local
  `gcloud auth application-default login`); optional base64 SA JSON
  **`GCP_SA_KEY`** for hosts without ADC, and REQUIRED to sign video upload URLs
  off Cloud Run. A few rows written before the move to GCS still name an older
  external image host: they render unoptimised (`lib/media/image-hosts.ts`), the
  storage sweep never deletes them, the OG proxy (`api/og-image`, gated by
  `lib/og-image.ts`) accepts only our own bucket, and `next.config.ts`
  `remotePatterns` lists only `storage.googleapis.com` and `images.unsplash.com`.
  Copying those files into GCS and rewriting the rows is an open data task, not a
  code change. Bucket needs CORS (PUT from the app origin) for direct video uploads.
  **`GCS_PRIVATE_BUCKET`** names a SECOND, private bucket (public access
  prevention on, uniform access, the runtime service account with object
  admin on it) for WhatsApp chat media, which is never written to the public
  one and is read only through `/api/dashboard/inbox/media/[messageId]`.
  Cloud Build passes `_GCS_PRIVATE_BUCKET` (empty by default, so a trigger
  without it stores no chat media rather than storing it publicly);
  `docs/gcp-ci-cd.md` names the bucket per environment. It also stages Refine
  with Mink AI results until they are paid for, under `refine-stage/{DB_NAME}/`
  (one prefix per database, because dev and staging share one database and
  one bucket, and local development uses that bucket with `storemink_local`);
  each environment's stage sweep lists only its own database's prefix.
  Without it Refine is not offered and the route refuses
  (`refine_not_configured`). It also holds Mink AI chat attachments under
  `stores/{store}/mink-attachments/{DB_NAME}/` (one folder per database, for
  the same reason); without it the composer offers no attachments and
  `/api/mink/attachments/[attachmentId]` answers 503. Local development sets it to
  `storemink-chat-media` to test Refine, which is safe for the same reason;
  two laptops whose databases are both `storemink_local` must not run the
  stage sweep against that bucket at the same time.
- **Image matting** (Change background): **`IMAGE_MATTING_URL`** is the
  private `storemink-image-matting` Cloud Run service (https, or plain http to
  localhost for `node services/image-matting/server.mjs`). Unset = the button
  is not offered. On Cloud Run the runtime account mints a Google identity
  token for it (it holds `roles/run.invoker` on the service); outside
  production the client asks `gcloud auth print-identity-token`, so a
  developer signed in to gcloud can set it in `.env.local` and use the
  deployed service. Cloud Build passes `_IMAGE_MATTING_URL`; one service in
  storemink-prod serves dev and prod.
- **Gemini / Vertex AI**: AI copy generation (`lib/ai/gemini.ts`, dual backend).
  **Backend precedence: the free Gemini Developer API key wins whenever one is
  set** — so **local + staging set `GEMINI_API_KEY`** (a Google AI Studio key,
  free) and their AI costs nothing; **production omits `GEMINI_API_KEY` and sets
  `GCP_PROJECT_ID`** so `callGemini` routes through **Vertex AI** via Application
  Default Credentials (ADC — no API key; automatic on Cloud Run) at
  **`GCP_LOCATION`** (default `global`). (An env with BOTH set prefers the free
  key.) Same request/response shape both ways; callers see the unchanged
  `{text,error}` contract. **`GEMINI_MODEL`** (default
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`) accepts only a Flash-Lite id, optionally
  version-pinned (`-001`, `-09-2026`, `-preview-…`); anything else, including
  the old `gemini-2.5-flash` (whose Vertex retirement date was 20 Oct 2026),
  is ignored with one `ai.generate: model override ignored` warning per
  process. **`GEMINI_FALLBACK_MODEL`** (default `gemini-3.5-flash`) accepts
  only a Flash id. Cloud Build sets neither, so deployments use the defaults;
  a local `.env` still naming gemini-2.5-flash should drop the line. On Vertex
  the main model runs at `GCP_LOCATION` (global; Cloud Build sets it) and the
  fallback at `MINK_FALLBACK_LOCATION` (asia-south1, read through
  `getMinkConfig()`), the pool Mink chat already fails over to; the Developer
  API has no location. Each attempt has 30 s (`GEMINI_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT_MS`,
  token, request and reply inside it) and honours a caller's signal. A 408,
  429, 5xx, network failure or timeout gets one attempt on the fallback, and
  so does a 400, 403 or 404 on the main model (logged as `ai.generate: main
model refused`, logError); the fallback is final, so the worst case is about
  a minute. Requests use LOW thinking (`thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel`, the
  shape `conversation-namer.ts` runs live through @google/genai) with 1,024
  tokens of headroom on top of the caller's answer budget; JSON replies use
  `responseJsonSchema` (lowercase JSON Schema), the Help assistant, Help search
  and the Help console's AI command included. ⚠ Not yet called live on this
  path (no paid calls in wave 1): the first owner-approved run should do one
  description, one SEO reply and one coupon email on Vertex and read the
  `ai.generate: ok` line's model and location. Vertex needs `google-auth-library` +
  `roles/aiplatform.user` on the runtime credentials (see
  `docs/gcp-migration-phase4-cloud-run.md` §3). Mink AI embeddings use the same backend
  precedence, credentials and Vertex address rule (`vertexHost`: us and eu
  through their regional-endpoint hosts, `global` through
  aiplatform.googleapis.com) through `lib/help/embeddings.ts`, with
  **`GEMINI_EMBEDDING_MODEL`** defaulting to `gemini-embedding-2` (served only
  through Vertex's `embedContent`; the former `gemini-embedding-001` is capped at
  five requests a minute, see §21) and a fixed
  768-dimensional schema contract. **`HELP_VECTOR_MIN_SIMILARITY`** optionally
  overrides the conservative `0.55` semantic-match floor (0–1); leave it unset
  until the retrieval evaluation set justifies a tuned value.
  The separate dashboard-agent foundation in `lib/mink/` is **Vertex-only** and
  uses the official `@google/genai` SDK with ADC; it never falls back to an API
  key. Its global runtime is enabled when **`MINK_AI_ENABLED` is unset**;
  **`MINK_AI_ENABLED=false`** is the explicit shutdown, while the independent
  legacy store invitation is ignored; staff permissions and human approvals remain enforced. It reads
  **`MINK_VERTEX_MODEL`** (default `gemini-3.7-flash`),
  **`MINK_VERTEX_LOCATION`** (fallback `GCP_LOCATION`, then `global`), plus
  bounded optional limits **`MINK_MAX_STEPS_PER_RUN`** (12),
  **`MINK_MAX_TOOL_CALLS_PER_RUN`** (16),
  **`MINK_MAX_PARALLEL_READ_TOOLS`** (4), and
  **`MINK_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`** (2048), **`MINK_IMAGE_MODEL`**
  (`gemini-nano-banana-2.1` since 25 Oct 2026, cloudbuild
  `_MINK_IMAGE_MODEL`; another model is sent no thinking level) and **`MINK_IMAGE_LOCATION`** (`global`; still an
  independent override from the chat location), plus reliability controls
  **`MINK_MAX_MODEL_RETRIES`** (2, bounded 0–3), **`MINK_RUN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`**
  (180, bounded 15–300), **`MINK_FIRST_CHUNK_SECONDS`** and
  **`MINK_STREAM_IDLE_SECONDS`** (20 each, bounded 5–120), and the fallback
  **`MINK_FALLBACK_MODEL`** (`gemini-3.5-flash`; "off" or empty disables it,
  and anything but a Gemini id reads as off) at **`MINK_FALLBACK_LOCATION`**
  (`asia-south1`), where voice chat turns start unless
  **`MINK_VOICE_ON_FALLBACK`** is "false"/"0"; see "Mink keeps answering when its model is busy". Tool routing reads
  **`MINK_TOOL_ROUTING`** (on unless "false"/"0"), **`MINK_LITE_MODEL`** (default
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`; anything but a Flash-Lite id falls back to it) and
  **`MINK_LITE_ROUTING`** (off unless "true"/"1"); see "Mink tool routing". The dashboard layout reads the private
  flag server-side: enabled sessions use the SSE client and durable alpha
  records; disabled sessions keep the canned placeholder. Reported or partial
  token usage receives a versioned provider-cost estimate; unavailable usage
  stays null/Unknown rather than looking free. `charged_credits` remains zero,
  so this build does not bill customers.
  Mink microphone transcription uses the one platform selection in
  `mink_voice_settings`: Google Chirp 3 calls Cloud Speech-to-Text V2 with the
  same ADC project and **`MINK_CHIRP_LOCATION`** (default `us`, where Chirp 3
  language-agnostic transcription is generally available), while
  Sarvam Saaras v4 requires server-only **`SARVAM_API_KEY`**. The Cloud Run
  service account holds least-privilege **`roles/speech.client`** to call
  Speech-to-Text. Neither credential is exposed to the dashboard.
  Theme Studio reads **`THEME_STUDIO_PROVIDER`** (code default `fake`, the offline
  test provider; `vertex-gemini` sends new runs to the allowlisted models
  and must not be set until the dedicated worker job exists — §4
  `api/internal/theme-studio/runs`), **`THEME_STUDIO_GENERATION_ENABLED`**
  (`false` stops new Studio runs without affecting merchant Mink),
  **`THEME_STUDIO_CAPTURE_ENABLED`** (code default false; enables catalog-picture
  queueing only after the separate Chromium capture job and scheduler exist),
  **`THEME_STUDIO_DISABLED_MODELS`** (comma-separated model KEYS to switch
  off; ★ the EMERGENCY SWITCH for one model, kept although it looks unused:
  the new-theme form hides a disabled model, queueing a run, revision or
  answer on it is refused, a run already queued fails as `model_disabled`,
  and a design review on it fails its tries and stops the theme as
  `qa_provider_failed`; `gemini-3.8-flash` is also the per-photo checker
  (`THEME_IMAGE_REVIEW_MODEL_KEY`), so switching it off leaves Theme Studio
  photos unchecked, which stops a theme at its final check
  (`image_check_required`, TS-1B), and leaves the storefront revamp's photo
  and product-photo checks unreviewed (`lib/mink/revamp/photos.ts`,
  `products.ts`). Set it with `gcloud run services update` and
  `--update-env-vars`, no build; ⚠ the next deploy's `--set-env-vars`
  replaces the whole environment and drops it unless it is added to
  `cloudbuild.yaml`, though the new revision no longer makes passed checks
  old, because evidence binds to the commit (TS-3C)),
  **`THEME_STUDIO_DAILY_SPEND_USD`** (per-operator rolling-24h
  estimated-spend ceiling; in code none unless set to a positive number;
  `cloudbuild.yaml` sets `50` since the Theme Studio release, owner-approved
  24 Oct 2026, 23:55 IST. Past it, starting a theme, Retry, answering the
  AI's questions, asking for a change and a photo run are refused with "You
  have reached today's Theme Studio spending limit. Try again tomorrow." It
  never stops a build already running: automatic repairs and fill rounds
  count toward the total but are never refused, design reviews are neither
  counted nor refused, and the offline provider is exempt. A trigger
  substitution overrides the default), and
  **`THEME_STUDIO_AUTO_QA_ENABLED`** (code default false and effective only
  with capture enabled), and **`THEME_STUDIO_PERFORMANCE_REQUIRED`** (code
  default false; `true` makes `browser.performance` a required gate: LCP
  ≤ 3 s and CLS < 0.1 at phone390 and desktop1440, judged from the
  automatic capture). Cloud Build explicitly sets the provider to
  `vertex-gemini` and enables generation, capture and automatic QA in
  production (the file's defaults; since 2026-10-10 the dev trigger sets the
  offline provider and switches all three off, so dev builds no themes);
  both worker schedules were deployed and smoke-checked on 2026-09-29.
  Preview tokens are signed with
  **`THEME_STUDIO_PREVIEW_SECRET`** when set, otherwise with a key derived
  from `CRON_SECRET` under a purpose label; with neither, previews refuse.
  Acceptance evidence is bound to **`THEME_STUDIO_BUILD_ID`** when set and
  not empty, otherwise to Cloud Run's `K_REVISION`. Cloud Build sets it to
  the commit (`COMMIT_SHA`, TS-3C, plan P3), so a settings-only revision or a
  re-run of the same commit never makes evidence old, but ANY new commit that
  deploys does, a docs-only or baseline-only one included (a
  `schema-fingerprint.json` commit to `main` deploys production; `[skip ci]` in
  its message skips the build). A manual
  `gcloud builds submit` has no commit and sets it empty, so the app uses `K_REVISION` and
  every new revision makes evidence old, as before. The first deploy
  carrying P3 changes the id from a revision name to a commit; like any code
  deploy, ready themes then re-check once at Publish. ⚠ A settings-only
  change to what the checks require (for example
  `THEME_STUDIO_PERFORMANCE_REQUIRED`) no longer expires passed checks
  either: press Check again on ready themes before publishing;
  the server stage fetches preview pages from **`THEME_STUDIO_ACCEPTANCE_ORIGIN`**
  when set, otherwise `http://127.0.0.1:$PORT`.
  Dedicated private services set **`THEME_STUDIO_WORKER_ONLY=true`** and
  **`THEME_STUDIO_WORKER_ROLE=generation|qa`**. They run one lane per request,
  bound Sharp/DB resources and accept the separate application secret header
  behind OIDC; these settings must not be applied to the merchant web service.
  Their **`THEME_STUDIO_BUILD_ID`** is the serving web's build (the commit
  since P3, or the web's serving revision when that is empty), not the worker
  revision. See `docs/theme-studio-worker-rollout.md` for first scheduler routing.
  Theme Studio's manual `theme-studio:model-check` uses ADC plus **`THEME_STUDIO_GCP_PROJECT_ID`**
  (fallback `GCP_PROJECT_ID`) and **`THEME_STUDIO_VERTEX_LOCATION`** (default
  `global`). Exact provider ids can be overridden only to a dated/versioned id
  in the SAME model family with the model-specific
  **`THEME_STUDIO_GEMINI_38_FLASH_MODEL`** and
  **`THEME_STUDIO_GEMINI_31_PRO_MODEL`** variables after verification in the
  target project. These do not configure merchant Mink; since Phase 3 the
  same project/location variables configure the Studio model worker.
  The Studio image client (Track 3) uses the same project, its own
  **`THEME_STUDIO_IMAGE_LOCATION`** (default `global`) and
  **`THEME_STUDIO_IMAGE_MODEL`** (`gemini-nano-banana-2.1`, cloudbuild
  `_THEME_STUDIO_IMAGE_MODEL`), which may pin a published version of it, or
  name the `gemini-3-pro-image` family as the owner's rollback; anything else
  throws.
  The storefront revamp (§ Mink storefront revamp) reads
  **`MINK_REVAMP_PROVIDER`** (`lib/mink/revamp/provider.ts`, the one reader
  every step takes its client from, so a run never mixes a fake plan with paid
  photos): `fake` (trimmed, any case) runs the offline planner and the fake
  image and review clients at no cost, for local development,
  `npm run revamp:live-check` and the opt-in `e2e.local` suite
  (`MINK_REVAMP_LOCAL_TEST=1`); anything else, and unset, is Vertex.
  `cloudbuild.yaml` never sets it, so dev and production always use the real
  models. Its planner, photographs and photo review use the Theme Studio
  Vertex settings and shared provider capacity above
  (`THEME_STUDIO_GCP_PROJECT_ID` or `GCP_PROJECT_ID`,
  `THEME_STUDIO_VERTEX_LOCATION`, `THEME_STUDIO_IMAGE_LOCATION`,
  `THEME_STUDIO_IMAGE_MODEL`; `THEME_STUDIO_DISABLED_MODELS` switching off the
  reviewer keeps the photos unreviewed), its product studio photos Mink's own
  `MINK_IMAGE_MODEL` / `MINK_IMAGE_LOCATION`, its stored photos `GCS_BUCKET`
  (unset, a revamp with photos to draw fails as `internal`), its
  budget the allowance `MINK_CHARGE_CREDITS` selects, and its run route and kick
  `CRON_SECRET` (the kick goes to the current request's origin, else
  `PLATFORM_URL`, from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`). `THEME_STUDIO_PROVIDER` and
  `THEME_STUDIO_GENERATION_ENABLED` do not apply to it; `MINK_AI_ENABLED=false`
  stops it (the run route claims nothing, the sweep does nothing).
- **Razorpay** (§18, §16): two SEPARATE credential sets. Per-store BYO gateway
  creds live in the DB (`store_payment_providers`, encrypted with env
  **`PAYMENT_CRED_KEY`** — 32-byte base64; generate with
  `openssl rand -base64 32`). The PLATFORM's own account (AI-credit purchases
  only) is env **`RAZORPAY_KEY_ID`** / **`RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET`**. Cron routes
  (`/api/cron/*`) require **`CRON_SECRET`** (Cloud Scheduler sends it as an
  `Authorization: Bearer` header).
- **WhatsApp** (docs/whatsapp-commerce-plan.md; Phase 0 as of 2026-10-08):
  the webhook reads **`WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN`** (ours — a high-entropy string
  pasted into the Meta console, used only for the GET handshake) and
  **`WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET`** (Meta's, signs every POST). ⚠ They are two
  different secrets for two different proofs — the token proves we own the
  URL, the secret proves a delivery came from Meta — and both are per
  environment, since a Meta app has exactly one callback URL (dev and prod are
  two Meta apps). With either unset the route answers 503 — deliveries carry
  data (orders, opt-outs, statuses) a silent ack would lose, so Meta is told
  to retry. Wired in `cloudbuild.yaml` since 2026-10-08
  (`_WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET_SECRET`, `_WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN_SECRET`, defaults
  `*_STAGING`; the prod trigger overrides to `*_PROD`) — the Secret Manager
  entries were created FIRST because Cloud Run refuses a revision whose
  `--set-secrets` names a missing secret. Dev and prod are two Meta apps
  (`1045672501851798` / `2663634187475548`), so **`WHATSAPP_APP_ID`** and
  **`WHATSAPP_CONFIG_ID`** (Embedded Signup; set on the dev trigger since
  2026-10-13, empty on prod until the production app has a configuration) are public identifiers riding as plain substitutions.
  `whatsappConnectConfigured()` needs app id + secret + config id, and the
  Channels card disables Connect without all three rather than opening a
  popup the server cannot finish. `npm run whatsapp:smoke`
  takes `WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN` + `WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID` from the shell
  only, never from `.env`; `WHATSAPP_GRAPH_VERSION` defaults to `v26.0`.
- **POS** (§22): the `/pos` device + operator cookies are HMAC-signed with env
  **`POS_SESSION_SECRET`** (any high-entropy string; `openssl rand -base64 32`).
  Required for the register to work; when unset, cookie VERIFY returns null
  (never throws) so /pos falls back to the login gate rather than 500ing.
  **That graceful degradation covers VERIFY only — MINTING a cookie cannot
  degrade**, so with the secret absent `authorizeThisDevice` / `pairDevice` /
  `posLoginWithPin` are dead. They now check `posSessionConfigured()` and return
  `POS_SECRET_MISSING_ERROR` instead of throwing a raw 500 (staging ran without
  the secret until 2026-07-27 — it was never added to `cloudbuild.yaml` — and
  every "Authorize this device" click 500'd). `registerDevice` also SIGNS BEFORE
  IT INSERTS: insert-then-sign left an orphan `pos_devices` row per failure, and
  those rows count against `PLAN_LIMITS.posDevicesPerLocation`, so a broken
  deployment eventually reported a bogus "already has 5 authorized devices".
  Deploy wiring is per-env (`_POS_SESSION_SECRET_SECRET` → the
  `POS_SESSION_SECRET_STAGING`/`_PROD` Secret Manager entries) — see
  `docs/gcp-ci-cd.md`.
- **Google Maps** (signup location step, §19): **`NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY`**
  — a Maps JavaScript API key from Google Cloud. Needs a billing account with a
  card even to stay inside the free allowance, and the key is public by nature
  (it ships to the browser), so restrict it by HTTP referrer to the app's hosts
  and enable only Maps JavaScript + Geocoding. **Entirely optional at runtime**:
  `app/platform/signup/location-picker.tsx` renders the map only when the key is
  present and supports a complete plain form when it is absent or rejected.
  Docker/Cloud Build pass `_NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY` into the client
  build; set this browser-restricted public key in each deployment trigger.
  Enable Maps JavaScript and Geocoding APIs in its project. Current-device
  geolocation first uses Google for street/area/PIN components, with bounded
  timeouts and a callback-based loader; BigDataCloud remains a browser-only
  locality fallback. Missing address fields are named explicitly for manual
  completion. Never infer a building number or PIN from a city alone.

- **Search-engine indexing** (`lib/seo/search-engines.ts`; full runbook in
  `docs/seo-indexing.md`): only the **production apex** is indexable —
  `SEARCH_INDEXABLE` in `lib/store/host.ts` (`ROOT_DOMAIN === "storemink.com" &&
NEXT_PUBLIC_NOINDEX !== "1"`) is the single gate for `robots.ts` (non-prod →
  `Disallow: /`), `sitemap.ts` (non-prod → empty), AND both notify channels, so
  staging/previews are auto-`noindex`d and never ping (no per-deploy flag; staging
  runs as `NODE_ENV=production` on Cloud Run, so the old `NODE_ENV` guard was
  insufficient). IndexNow needs no account (public key file `public/<key>.txt`;
  `INDEXNOW_KEY` overrides it, `INDEXNOW_FORCE=1` pings off-prod). Google Search
  Console submission is DORMANT until `GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_PROPERTY` (e.g.
  `sc-domain:storemink.com`) is set — auth is then the **runtime service account
  via ADC** (nothing to store; `cloudbuild.yaml` passes the property, prod trigger
  = `sc-domain:storemink.com`), or an explicit `GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_CREDENTIALS`
  key JSON for non-GCP hosts. One-time human setup: verify `storemink.com` as a
  Search Console Domain property (covers all `*.storemink.com`), add the
  `storemink-run@…` SA as a property user, enable the Search Console and Site
  Verification APIs, and create the `storemink-seo-refresh` Cloud Scheduler job.
  `lib/seo/store-indexing.ts` is the single store discovery pipeline: publish
  paths call it after commit, and `/api/cron/seo-refresh` registers the platform,
  help, POS, and themes sitemaps before reconciling every
  active/launched/non-demo store daily. StoreMink subdomains submit under the
  Domain property. A verified custom domain gets a Google META token in public
  `stores.settings`, an automatically verified URL-prefix property, and its own
  sitemap submission. Replacing or disconnecting that domain removes the public
  token first, then best-effort deletes the old Search Console property and the
  runtime service account's Site Verification ownership record so detached
  domains do not accumulate indefinitely. Google's META verification response is a complete HTML
  tag, but Next metadata accepts only its `content` value; the pipeline
  normalizes that value before storage and also repairs legacy full-tag values
  so the tag cannot be escaped inside another tag. Attempt/success/error
  timestamps are persisted;
  successful stores are refreshed at most weekly, failures retry daily and make
  the cron return 503 so Cloud Scheduler's three retries engage. Full setup and
  Google-controlled limitations: `docs/seo-indexing.md`.
  Search performance collection is a separate failure domain:
  `/api/cron/search-metrics` runs after sitemap reconciliation, queries the
  Search Analytics API, and never makes a metrics failure look like a sitemap
  failure. Platform subdomains all query the root Domain property through an
  anchored, regex-escaped page filter; custom domains query their URL-prefix
  property. Every response must be page-aggregated. CTR is derived, while
  position is stored as `position × impressions`. Source epochs preserve
  history and enforce inclusive PT ownership bounds when canonical domains
  change. The schema is service-role only; dashboard reads will use typed
  tenant-gated aggregates rather than direct table access.
  **A store's public origin is always selected by `storeOrigin(store)`.** Never
  use `custom_domain ?? subdomain`. The custom domain counts only once
  `settings.custom_domain_verified === true` and the effective plan is still
  entitled to custom domains, the same two gates `lookupStoreByHost`
  (`lib/store/resolve.ts`) applies when deciding whether to serve that domain. A
  lapsed timed plan therefore falls back to the working StoreMink subdomain in
  routing, canonical, robots, sitemap and notifications together.
  `saveCustomDomain` writes `custom_domain` while clearing the verified flag, so
  every merchant passes through a state where the store is served on its
  subdomain. Pointing canonical, `og:url`, robots `Host:`, sitemap `<loc>` or an
  IndexNow ping at that unverified domain makes Google follow an unreachable
  canonical and can drop the working URL as "Alternate page with proper
  canonical tag". `getStoreUrl()` and `getStoreOriginById()` both route through
  `storeOrigin()`; regression-tested in `lib/site.test.ts`. Related: a
  store-shaped host that resolves to no store (unclaimed subdomain, suspended
  store, unseeded demo) returns `Disallow: /` plus an empty sitemap instead of
  advertising StoreMink's platform URLs.
  **`app/sitemap.ts` emits no fabricated `lastmod`.** Each URL derives it from a
  real content timestamp or omits it, guarded by `app/sitemap.test.ts`. Products
  use `products.content_updated_at`
  (`seo_01_product_content_timestamp.sql`), a trigger-maintained column
  that moves only when a visitor-visible field changes. `updated_at` is bumped
  by `_recompute_stock_aggregate` on every sale and would claim a content change
  per purchase. Pages use `published_at`, not `updated_at`, because draft
  autosave advances `updated_at` while public HTML remains unchanged. (So a
  StoreMink block or lift, which moves `updated_at`, does not move a lastmod.)
  ★ `imageEntry` leaves out the takedown placeholder's path and any address in
  the blocked set (`blockedMedia()`, read once per store sitemap), so the
  sitemap never lists a blocked image or the placeholder; a blocked product,
  page, post or collection is already absent (the read policies hide it;
  convention 45).
- **★★ A NEW STORE IS CLOSED UNTIL ITS OWNER PRESSES GO LIVE (2026-10-07).**
  `stores.settings.launched` is ONE flag behind two things: search
  indexability (as before) and, now, the **storefront password page**.
  `isStoreLaunched` / `isDemoStore` / `isStoreSearchIndexable` /
  `isStorefrontGated` / `isThemePending` are pure predicates in
  `lib/store/launch-state.ts` (no imports, so the host resolver can read them
  without a cycle; `launch.ts` re-exports them). At creation a store was then
  pure theme seed (since 2026-10-11 it has no theme at all, below) — the same
  homepage, ~17 content pages and sample catalogue as every other store on
  that template — and until this change the flag flipped on the FIRST PUBLISH
  of anything (page, product, blog, CSV import, Mink publication), so a shop
  with no refund policy and the theme's placeholder homepage went public, and
  into Google, the moment its first product was saved.
  ★ **`markStoreLaunched()` has exactly one caller now: `launchStore` in
  `app/actions/launch-actions.ts`**, which re-runs the go-live checklist
  server-side (superadmin only — opening a shop is the owner's call, the §22
  owner-only rule), sets the flag, refreshes `STORE_TAG`, emits
  `store.launched` (both channels, not configurable) and only THEN calls
  `notifyStoreContentPublished()`. That hook no longer launches; on an
  unlaunched store it returns without submitting anything, because the pages
  behind the password redirect and robots/sitemap already say `noindex`.
  ★ **The checklist is predicates over real rows, never tick boxes**
  (`lib/store/launch-checklist-rules.ts` pure + `launch-checklist.ts` reads).
  ★★ REQUIRED IS FIVE TASKS, GROUPED (owner, 2026-10-11: nine rows read as a
  wall), and grouping drops no requirement — every step is still its own
  predicate and a grouped task is done only when all its steps are, in order:
  (1) `phone` "Verify your mobile number" — the owner's verified mobile (a
  superadmin admins row with `phone_verified_at`, never bare `phone`, which
  invited staff type unchecked), verified inline; (2) `theme` "Choose your
  storefront theme" — `!isThemePending(store)`, read from the store row in
  hand, so it costs no query and every store without the key has it done;
  (3) `products` "Add your first product" — one published non-sample product
  (samples are named "… (Sample)" and seed as drafts); (4) `business` "Add your
  business and delivery details" — two STEPS: business name, address, email
  and phone in `store_billing_settings` (→ Taxes & invoices), and Shipping &
  delivery saved once; (5) `policies` "Publish your store policies" — four
  STEPS, Terms & Conditions, Refund & Cancellation, Shipping and Privacy
  published (the Settings → Policies registry, pinned equal by test), one
  destination. `groupedTask()` builds a grouped task from its steps, so its
  tick, link and refusal cannot disagree with them: the button goes to the
  first unfinished step's page (steps sharing one page share one button), and
  the go-live refusal names outstanding tasks with their open steps in
  brackets ("Publish your store policies (Refund & Cancellation, Privacy)").
  `launchStore` re-runs the whole checklist. RECOMMENDED, never blocking: homepage edited
  since seeding (updated_at more than a minute after created_at), logo, sample
  products removed, payments connected (COD works out of the box, and Free has
  no online payments, so requiring it would mean no Free store ever opens),
  GSTIN, custom domain. Items on a plan that lacks the feature link to Plans.
  ★ **The gate lives in `requireStorefrontStore()`**, not the proxy (no DB
  there) and not the layout (a layout redirect does not abort a concurrently
  rendering child page — the §3 rule). For a gated store it dynamically
  imports `lib/store/storefront-access.ts`, whose request-memoized
  `storefrontAccess()` answers `open | unlocked | locked`: unlocked for a
  visitor carrying a valid `sm_store_pass` grant, or for the Website
  Builder's preview iframe (`x-sm-preview` header AND an admin session);
  locked otherwise → `redirect("/password")`. ★★ THE OWNER IS GATED TOO
  (owner's decision, 2026-10-08): a first version let any signed-in admin
  through, which hid the password page from the one person who needs to
  understand it. Shopify's rule applies — everyone, owner included, types
  the password, which sits on Dashboard Home beside Go live. The builder
  preview is the one exception, or the builder is blind until launch. The layout renders a locked visitor a minimal
  shell (brand tokens, no header/footer/cart, since every link in them would
  lead back to the password page). `/password` (`(storefront)/(pages)/password`,
  reserved in `RESERVED_PAGE_SLUGS` and `STOREFRONT_CODE_ROUTES`) does NOT
  call `requireStorefrontStore()`.
  ★★ **A STORE WITH NO THEME SHOWS "STORE IN PROGRESS" (2026-10-11).** Signup
  installs no theme (§11), so after the password check `requireStorefrontStore()`
  sends every visitor of an `isThemePending` store — the owner included, and
  the builder preview too — to `/in-progress`
  (`STOREFRONT_IN_PROGRESS_PATH`, `(storefront)/(pages)/in-progress`, also in
  `RESERVED_PAGE_SLUGS` and `STOREFRONT_CODE_ROUTES`). Order is host 404 →
  password → theme, so a locked visitor never learns the store has no theme;
  `/password` sends an unlocked visitor to `/`, which then lands here. The page
  is the password page's card: the brand name or logo, "This store is being set
  up. Please check back soon." and an "Are you the owner? Choose a theme in your
  dashboard" link to `/dashboard/storefront`, `noindex`. It does not call
  `requireStorefrontStore()` (that would loop); it repeats the three checks
  itself and redirects to `/` once a theme is chosen. The layout picks its
  shell with `storefrontShell(store, access)` — "bare" for a locked visitor or
  a pending store, "full" otherwise. A pending store is never launched (the
  checklist's theme task blocks Go live), so this page is only ever seen
  behind the password. Stores without the key never see it.
  ★ **The password is a secret, and `stores.settings` is anon-readable**
  (§5.9), so it lives in service-only `store_access`
  (`20261007_0170_store_access`; `password`, `password_version`), created on
  first read with INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING + read-the-winner. The grant
  (`lib/store/storefront-grant.ts`) is an HMAC token bound to store id +
  password version, keyed by `STOREFRONT_PASSWORD_SECRET` or derived from
  `CRON_SECRET` with a purpose label (the Theme Studio preview-token
  construction), 7-day host-only httpOnly cookie; regenerating the password
  bumps the version and every old grant dies on the next request.
  `unlockStorefront` (`app/actions/storefront-access-actions.ts`) is
  host-derived, rate-limited per visitor and per store, compares in constant
  time, and only follows a same-origin `next`.
  ★ **Every public WRITE refuses while locked**: `storefrontClosedRefusal()`
  sits beside `demoStoreRefusal()` in placeOrder, enquiries, newsletter,
  reviews, blog reactions/comments, customer blog submissions and account
  creation; `/api/storefront/search` answers empty; `getCheckoutConfig` carries
  `closed`. A visitor who entered the password is NOT refused — that is the
  owner testing their own checkout, which is what the password is for.
  ★ **Absence of the flag means LAUNCHED** — pre-existing stores have no key,
  and treating them as unlaunched would now put a password page in front of
  live shops; `createStore` writes `launched: false` explicitly. Migration 0170
  also opens any `launched: false` store that has ever taken an order, so no
  trading shop wakes up behind a password. Demo stores (`settings.demo`) are
  never gated and never indexed. A merchant's store gets no theme SAMPLE
  products or categories at all since 31 Oct 2026 (§11, "No sample
  catalogue"); demo stores still seed them, published
  (`applyTheme`'s `publishSampleProducts`).
  **Dashboard Home is ONE card while the store is closed** (`setup-guide.tsx`,
  the Shopify setup-guide shape, redesigned 2026-10-08 after the first version
  ran to three cards and six tiles): a slim `PlanTag` beside the greeting
  ("Free plan · Upgrade", with the next plan's unlocks in its title, derived
  from `PLAN_LIMITS` via `lib/plans/upgrade-summary.ts`); then the card whose
  HEAD is the store password (Copy / New / Preview) and the Go live button,
  and whose body is the five required tasks as an accordion ("x of 5 done") —
  exactly one open, the first unfinished, showing its description and a button
  that goes there (`LaunchChecklistItem.action`); a grouped task lists its
  steps inside, each with its own tick, Done/To do text for screen readers and
  an "n of m" count, so the card stays five rows long without hiding a
  requirement. **Recommended renders only once every
  required task is done, and folds** (collapsed by default with a count).
  Mink's prompt, the six setup tiles and "All caught up" return once the store
  is open. `setup-guide.test.tsx` pins the open-first-unfinished, hidden-then-
  folded and owner-only rules. ★ **The card's look (the "Aurora hero",
  chosen 2026-11-10; presentation only, no behaviour changed)**: the password,
  Go live and a progress ring share one band over a soft indigo, violet and
  sky wash (`setup-guide.module.css`: the wash, a blurred ribbon, a dot grid
  from `@sm`, a gradient seam, and Go live's sheen, one sweep that ends
  within 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2), and only with motion allowed). The open task is a tinted panel with a
  gradient left bar and a gradient icon tile; unfinished tasks show their
  number in the ring. Go live is a grey well until the store is ready, then
  an indigo-to-violet button with a halo; the ring turns green at 100%.
  Copy, New and Preview are 44px tall on a touch screen. Every layout follows
  the CARD's width (container queries), since the Mink AI panel can squeeze
  it to about 230px. ⚠ The hero's padding, ring and gap are tied to the task
  list's padding and icon column (`HERO_SLOT`/`HERO_ROW` against
  `ICON_SLOT`/`TITLE_INDENT`), so the ring sits on the task icons' centre and
  the hero's text on the task titles' left edge; change one side and the
  other must move with it. No Help Centre update: no merchant step changed.
  **The mobile task is done IN the card**: for a
  viewer who is one of the store's real owners (`ownerCanVerifyPhone`, an
  admins row with role superadmin, which a platform operator's synthetic
  superadmin profile is not) it renders `VerifyPhoneForm` (next/dynamic, so
  the phone library and Firebase phone sign-in load only when the task is
  opened), then refreshes and opens the next task. Anyone else is told the
  owner verifies their own number, because verifying THEIR number would not
  complete the task. ★★ `VerifyPhoneForm`
  (`app/dashboard/components/verify-phone-form.tsx`, shared with Account
  settings) proves the number on the SECONDARY in-memory Firebase app, the
  POS customer-verification pattern: a fresh reCAPTCHA per send, the code
  confirmed there, the ID token handed to `confirmVerifiedPhone`, which
  requires a phone sign-in under five minutes old, stores the token's E.164
  number (never the browser's) with `phone_verified_at = now()`, and deletes
  only a just-created, phone-only identity that holds no StoreMink role. The
  merchant's own login and session are never touched, which is what lets a
  number that is also a shopper's identity verify. A save that fails after
  Firebase accepted the code keeps the proof, so **Try again** needs no new
  code (pinned and mutation-checked in `verify-phone-form.test.tsx`). The `store.created` welcome says the store is READY, not live, that its
  address shows a store-in-progress page until a theme is chosen, and lists
  the same five tasks in the same order at their real routes. Help:
  `20261007_0171_launch_checklist_help` edits the signup and setup guides in
  place; `20261008_0173_owner_password_help` corrects the setup guide to say
  the owner enters the password too; `20261010_0182_signup_plan_and_themes_help`
  edits the signup, setup, account and plans guides for the three-step
  signup, the checklist's mobile task and themes chosen from the dashboard,
  and publishes "Change your storefront theme";
  `20261011_0183_storefront_theme_help` edits the signup, setup, theme,
  dashboard and first-product guides for the theme-less start, the
  store-in-progress page, Storefront under Online store and the five grouped
  tasks. ★ "Personalise your
  homepage" is measured from when the THEME last wrote the homepage
  (`settings.theme.homepageSeededAt`, falling back to the row's creation),
  through `homepageEditedSinceSeed` in lib/themes/switch-rules.ts, so a
  theme install, or the sample clean-up's link rewrite, that touches the
  homepage does not tick the task for the merchant. Full audit of the SEO half:
  `docs/seo-action-plan.md`.
- **StoreMink's own brand identity for schema lives in
  `lib/seo/brand-identity.ts`** — one Organization node (`sameAs` for the
  LinkedIn/YouTube/Instagram profiles, `contactPoint`, `address`) emitted from
  BOTH the apex and `help.storemink.com` under a single `@id`, plus the matching
  visible footer links. Two hand-written copies would drift, and a contradictory
  entity is worse than an absent one. **Only public profile URLs belong in
  `sameAs`** — never a `/admin/` dashboard URL.
- **Each merchant has a separate Organization entity** at its canonical
  `${origin}/#organization` (`(storefront)/components/structured-data.tsx`). It
  emits the configured brand name/legal name/logo/blurb, public email/phone and
  valid Instagram/YouTube URLs; the store WebSite, Product and BlogPosting nodes
  reference that same `@id`. Missing merchant data is omitted rather than
  replaced with StoreMink/WholeSip identity.

## 8. Multi-tenant rollout status (as of 2026-07)

Phases 1–3c complete: schema + RLS + store resolution + signup journey +
per-store branding + platform admin console are live on branch `multi-tenant`.
Legacy WholeSip fallback remains until all traffic moves to real store hosts.

## 9. Product direction (owner's vision — keep in mind for every design decision)

- **storemink.com is the soul.** `storemink.com/dashboard` (platform operator
  console) sees _everything_: all features plus platform-only controls — Stores
  management (suspend/unsuspend, plan upgrade/downgrade), operators, etc.
  `{slug}.storemink.com/dashboard` sees only that store's own features/settings.
- **Everything must be settings-based.** Feature behavior is configured per
  store, not hardcoded. Canonical example — blogs: a store can toggle (a) whether
  customers may submit blogs at all, and (b) whether submissions need admin
  approval or publish directly, and it owns its blog categories/tags outright
  (convention #10). Every feature should be built with this kind of per-store
  configurability from the start. **The framework for this now exists**
  (`lib/settings/`, rendered on each feature's own settings page — blogs →
  `/dashboard/blogs/settings`; see convention #9), and blogs is the first
  consumer.
- **The website is dashboard-editable** (convention #11): the homepage, the
  former hardcoded static pages, and merchant-built custom pages are ALL per-store
  data (sections + custom HTML/CSS/JS) edited in the Website Builder
  (`/dashboard/builder`) with live preview and a draft → publish workflow;
  header/footer nav is per-store too (`/dashboard/navigation`). Merchant JS is
  sandbox-isolated. Phase 4 completed this fold-in — only genuinely interactive
  routes (shop, cart, blogs, enquiries, profile) remain in code.
- **Templates**: at signup the merchant picks a storefront template (filter by
  business category + free/paid, preview, plan-gated — e.g. "For STARTER and
  above"). Multiple visual templates are a planned core feature; today there is
  one storefront with per-store branding.
- **Checkout (COD, built)**: a signed-in shopper places a Cash-on-Delivery order
  from `/checkout` → `placeOrder` (`app/actions/checkout-actions.ts`), stored in
  `orders`/`order_items` (`orders_table.sql`) and listed at
  `/dashboard/orders`. See convention #12 for the checkout security model.
- **Deliberately later phases** (not built yet, by choice): online **payments**
  (BYO gateway — merchant connects own Razorpay/Cashfree; checkout is COD-only
  for now), merchant subscription billing for StoreMink plans.
- **WholeSip cleanup is nearly done**: the product started as the WholeSip site
  and was converted into StoreMink. The hardcoded homepage/hero + static pages
  are migrated (Phase 4), and the `--wholesip-*` CSS tokens (→ `--sm-*`) and
  `WHOLESIP_STORE_ID` (→ `FALLBACK_STORE_ID`) are renamed. What remains is only
  the repo/dir name `wholesip`, the `brand/` dir, and the fallback store's own
  DB identity (a real store row named "WholeSip") — bigger/data-level, not code.
